title: Two same-named _AT Partials with the same static name build and pass
claim: Verdict: kept. One test holds `#include TEST_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE_AT(a, util)` and `#include TEST_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE_AT(b, util)`. Each `util.c` defines a static `util_helper` and a public function (`a_pub`, `b_pub`). The build compiles, links and passes (TESTED 1, PASSED 1). Ceedling writes `a/ceedling_partial_util_impl.{c,h}` and `b/ceedling_partial_util_impl.{c,h}` below `build/test/partials/test/test_collide/_t_/`. Their include guards differ (`GENB59956D4_A_CEEDLING_PARTIAL_UTIL_IMPL_H_CEEDLING` and `GEN7118F419_B_...`). PUBLIC mode leaves the static out of the generated source, so the shared static name never meets itself.

title: Same-named public or selected functions in two _AT modules fail at link
claim: Verdict: kept (inherent). Three variants fail with `multiple definition` at link, never at compile. (v2) both `util.c` define a public `util_pub`. (v1b) both public functions call `util_helper` and the test selects it with `TEST_PARTIAL_CONFIG_AT` for each module. (v3) both modules use `TEST_PARTIAL_PRIVATE_MODULE_AT`, which promotes the same-named statics. The fixture comment says the same. Directory qualification keeps the generated files apart but cannot keep the function names apart.

title: A variable name used by both same-named modules breaks compile or link
claim: Verdict: kept (inherent). When both `a/util.c` and `b/util.c` hold `static struct { int count; } s_ctx;`, the test fails to compile with `conflicting types for 'ceedling_partial_util_s_ctx_t'` and `conflicting types for 's_ctx'`. Both types headers (`a/` and `b/`) write `typedef struct { int count; } ceedling_partial_util_s_ctx_t;`. With a plain `static int s_count;` in both (no type) the build compiles and fails at link with `multiple definition`. With distinct variable names (`a_ctx`, `b_ctx`) it builds and passes. So the module-name-only type name collides only when the variable name also collides, and that variable collides without the type.

title: Mock Partials of same-named modules stay apart only through :mock_name_include_folder
claim: Verdict: kept (default on). `MOCK_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE_AT(a, util)` and `(b, util)` in one test build and pass. CMock names the lifecycle functions `a_Mockceedling_partial_util_interface_Init` and `b_...`, and the runner calls both. With `:cmock` ↳ `:mock_name_include_folder: FALSE` the same test fails at link with `multiple definition of Mockceedling_partial_util_interface_Init`, `_Verify` and `_Destroy`. The setting defaults to true in Ceedling and to false in CMock.

title: The module name in generated Partial type names carries no directory
claim: Verdict: kept. `Partials.type_name` folds `File.basename(module_name)`, so modules `a/util` and `b/util` both give `ceedling_partial_util_<variable>_t`. The experiment shows the same typedef name in both generated types headers. `PARTIAL_TYPE(util, s_ctx)` therefore cannot say which module it means.

title: A character a C identifier cannot hold becomes an underscore in Partial type names
claim: Verdict: kept. `CIdentifier.fold` replaces each `\W` character with `_`, one for one, and `Partials.type_name` applies it to the module's basename. `PARTIAL_TYPE` and `PARTIAL_LOCAL_TYPE` paste their arguments as tokens, so a test author writes the folded spelling (`my_sensor`), as the docs say.

title: A promoted function-scoped static is named from the function and variable, never the module
claim: Verdict: kept. The promoted name is `partial_<function>_<variable>` and carries no module part. File-scoped statics keep their own names and are declared `extern` in `_impl.h`. The docs promise uniqueness only among functions of one module. Two modules with a same-named function cannot be in one test in any case.

title: A Partial module name that is a predefined macro is replaced before it names the file
claim: Verdict: broken. In a GCC build the compiler predefines `unix` as 1. A test with `#include TEST_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE(unix)` and a `unix.c` module preprocesses to `#include "ceedling_partial_1_impl.h"`. Ceedling reads the directive as written and generates `ceedling_partial_unix_impl.{c,h}`. It also writes an empty `ceedling_partial_1_impl.h`. The test links without the module and fails with `undefined reference to 'unix_pub'`, under a notice that blames missing `#include` lines. `__PARTIALS_EXPAND(module)` expands the argument, and `_validate_module!` checks spelling only. This is the mechanism of #1460, which names the directory argument. The `_AT` module argument passes through `__PARTIALS_JOIN`, whose indirection also expands macros. That path was inferred and not built.

title: Generated Partial headers include their siblings by bare filename
claim: Verdict: kept, by the compiler's includer-directory rule. `a/ceedling_partial_util_impl.h` holds `#include "ceedling_partial_util_types.h"` and `a/ceedling_partial_util_impl.c` holds `#include "ceedling_partial_util_impl.h"`, with no directory. The test compile puts both `-I build/.../_t_/a` and `-I build/.../_t_/b` on the command line. Each bare include finds its own sibling only because GCC checks the includer's directory before the `-I` list. A resolver that skips the includer's directory would pick the first `-I` entry (`a/`) for `b/`'s include.

title: The runner of a test naming two same-named _AT Partials includes one impl header, by bare name
claim: Verdict: partly kept (observed, cause not traced). The test names `a/ceedling_partial_util_impl.h` and `b/ceedling_partial_util_impl.h`. Its generated runner holds one `#include "ceedling_partial_util_impl.h"` with no directory. The bare name resolves to `a/` by `-I` order. The test passes, since the runner needs neither header. I did not trace which step collapses the two includes. The runner spelling comes from `include.include_path || include.filename`.

title: Same-named modules named by directory stay distinct modules in the Partials config
claim: Verdict: kept. `_module_key` joins a qualified macro's directory segments to the module with `File.join`, so `./drv` and `drv` give one module and `a/util` and `b/util` give two. Validation rejects an empty or quoted module, a module carrying a path, and a directory that is empty, quoted, absolute, or holds `..`. The experiment confirms two distinct generated Partials for the two modules.

title: Generated Partial filenames for _AT macros carry the macro's directory, which the docs table omits
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The overview table lists `ceedling_partial_<module>_impl.h` and the sibling patterns. For `_AT` macros the file is `<dir>/ceedling_partial_<module>_impl.h`: `form_partial_filename` puts the directory first and the prefix on the basename. The unqualified macros name a file with no directory.

title: Partials are generated into a partials build directory
claim: Verdict: kept. Generated Partial files sit below `<build root>/test/partials/<test path>/_t_/`, one root per test, mirrored by directory for `_AT` macros.

title: A plain Partial build links only the Partial, never the module's own object
claim: Verdict: kept. The linker command for the same-named experiment lists the test object, `a/` and `b/` `ceedling_partial_util_impl.o`, the runner and Unity. No object of `src/a/util.c` or `src/b/util.c` is linked.

title: The unqualified Partial macro with two same-basename modules picks the first by search-path priority
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say the macros "expand into the unique names of the generated Partials header files". `TEST_PARTIAL_PUBLIC_MODULE(util)` with `src/a/util.c` and `src/b/util.c` names one Partial. Ceedling logs `Multiple files matched 'util.c' but chose 'src/a/util.c' by search-path priority` and the test passes against `a/`'s code. Only the `_AT` macros name two.

title: test:path matches a substring of the test's directory, not of its whole path
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say "tests whose path contains the given string". The code tests `File.dirname(test).include?(arg)` on the project-relative test path, with `\` turned into `/`. With tests in `test/unit`, `test/unit_extra` and `test/integration`: `test:path[unit]` ran 2 tests (substring, so `unit_extra` too), `test:path[nit]` ran 2, `test:path[t/in]` ran 1, `test:path[unit/]` found none (no trailing separator in a dirname), `test:path[test_foo.c]` found none (filename excluded) and `test:path[Test]` found none (case).

title: test:pattern matches a regular expression against the project-relative test path
claim: Verdict: kept. The code applies `test =~ /#{regex}/` to each collected test path. Collected paths are relative to the project, so `^test/unit/` matched one test and the absolute directory of the project is never part of the text (`test:path[gap-10]` found nothing).

title: test:<name> takes as much trailing path as needed and names every match when ambiguous
claim: Verdict: kept. With `test/unit/test_foo.c`, `test/integration/test_foo.c` and `test/unit_extra/test_foo.c`, `test:test_foo.c` stops with `Ambiguous file reference 'test_foo.c' found. Include more trailing path` and lists all three. `test:unit/test_foo.c` and `test:unit\test_foo.c` each run one test. The lookup is `PathMatcher` in strict mode.

title: The bullseye: and gcov: tasks reuse the test: name, pattern and path rules
claim: Verdict: kept. Both plugins resolve a single-file task with `TestTaskName.test_name` and `find_test_file_from_name`, so trailing-path disambiguation matches `test:`. Their `path` tasks use the same `File.dirname(test).include?` test, so the `test:path` limits apply to them too. Read only. I did not run these plugins.

title: ceedling paths:header does not exist; the task is paths:include
claim: Verdict: broken. The reference lists `ceedling paths:header`. Ceedling defines a `paths:<name>` task for each key of `:paths`, and the standard sections are test, source, include and support. `ceedling paths:header` ends with `Unrecognized build task`. `paths:include` lists the include paths. The getting-started page repeats the error by listing `files:*` variants under `paths:*`.

title: files:assembly exists even when assembly support is off
claim: Verdict: broken. Both command line pages say the task is only available when assembly support is enabled. The `files` namespace creates a task for each of tests, source, assembly, headers and support unconditionally. With `:test_build` ↳ `:use_assembly: FALSE` and no release assembly, `ceedling files:assembly` runs and prints `Assembly files: None`.

title: The Dependencies doc names a files:include task that does not exist
claim: Verdict: broken. The doc lists `files:include` as "Lists every header file Ceedling has found, including those from dependencies". The core defines `files:header` for that. `ceedling files:include` ends with `Unrecognized build task`. `paths:include` is real.

title: Dependency include directories and globs are added to the header file collection as literal entries
claim: Verdict: defect. `include_files` maps every `:includes` entry, whether a header, a directory or a glob, to a path below the artifact path. `Dependencies#config` and `#add_headers_and_sources` push all of them into `collection_all_headers`. With `:includes: [inc/**, single/one.h]`, `files:header` lists `dependencies/Vend/inc/**` as a header file.

title: A dependency's :artifact path skips :source and :fetch when :build is left out
claim: Verdict: broken. The docs say `:artifact` falls back to `:build`, and `:build` falls back to `:source`, then `:fetch`. The code reads `@paths[:artifact] || @paths[:build] || default_path`. A dependency with only `:source: ext/src` gets build `ext/src` but artifact `dependencies/<name>`. In the build, `:includes: [inc/**]` of such a dependency appears in `paths:include` as `dependencies/Vend/inc`, not `vendor_dep/inc`. A fix changes where artifacts are looked for, so it is a BreakingChanges candidate.

title: dependencies:clean misses a default path that a fetch used
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The doc says clean removes "every one of its working paths". `working_paths` returns the configured paths only (`@paths` less `:deploy`), and the default `dependencies/<name>` is used only when a path falls back to it. With only `:artifact: out` configured, fetch and source resolve to `dependencies/<name>` while clean removes only `out`. With only `:build: b`, clean removes only `b`. Fetch then sees a non-empty fetch path and skips.

title: Dependency artifacts resolve against the artifact path, absolute names stand, and ~ expands
claim: Verdict: kept. `artifact_at` standardizes the entry, which expands a leading `~`, then keeps an absolute path as written and joins any other below `artifact_path`.

title: dependencies:deploy copies dynamic libraries and executables beside the release executable by default
claim: Verdict: kept. The destination is `spec.deploy_path(File.dirname(PROJECT_RELEASE_BUILD_TARGET))`. The target lies below `<build root>/release/` (for example `build/release/project.out`), not in the artifacts directory.

title: Dependency fetch runs in the fetch path and build steps run in the source path
claim: Verdict: kept. Fetch steps run inside `spec.fetch_path` after it is created, so a relative archive `:source` is relative to the fetch path. Each build step runs in `spec.source_path`, and the source, build and artifact paths are created first. Both use `WorkingDir.chdir`.

title: Dependency :source artifacts join the include and source collections, not :paths :source
claim: Verdict: kept. `add_source_path` appends each `:source` directory to four include-style collections and its C files to `collection_all_source`. It does not touch `collection_paths_source`. The doc promises search paths and release sources only.

title: A :build_lib static library is built in :build and copied to :artifact when they differ
claim: Verdict: kept. The first `:static_libraries` entry is built at `<build path>/<entry>` and copied to `<artifact path>/<entry>` unless the two paths are equal. Object placement is GAP-04's.

title: files:dependencies lists every library and executable path, built or not
claim: Verdict: kept. The task prints the static libraries, dynamic libraries and executables of every spec. In the experiment it listed `dependencies/Vend/libvend.a` although nothing built it.

title: Mixin names resolve through user load paths, the project file's directory, then Unity's targets
claim: Verdict: kept. `Composinator#loadinate` appends `File.dirname(project_filepath)` and the built-in Unity targets directory to the user load paths and deduplicates by expanded path. `BUILTIN_MIXIN_LOAD_PATHS` holds the Unity `test/targets` directory.

title: Mixin and mixin-variable file paths are relative to the working directory
claim: Verdict: kept. Filepaths go to `File.exist?` as written, so they resolve against the working directory. The mixin directory fallback uses the project file's own directory.

title: A mixin simple name is told from a filepath by extension or the forward slash only
claim: Verdict: untestable here (Windows). `PathValidator#filepath?` returns true for a value with an extension or one containing `File::SEPARATOR`, which is `/` on every platform. The docs say "no path separator" and the project docs accept `\`. Whether a Windows `--mixin bar\base` (no extension) reaches this test unstandardized was not traced.

title: A mixin's list entries land before the base list, except tool arguments
claim: Verdict: kept. `RecursiveMerger` builds `mixin_val + config_val` for lists and `config_val + mixin_val` for `:tools` ↳ `<tool>` ↳ `:arguments`. A higher-priority mixin's `:paths` entries therefore come first. Search order inside the merged list is not changed afterwards.

title: Mixin load paths are searched top-down and each path tries every YAML extension
claim: Verdict: kept. `load_paths.product(yaml_extensions)` yields every extension of the first path before the next path.

title: A test suite needs :paths :include and/or TEST_INCLUDE_PATH, and no :include entry is required
claim: Verdict: kept. A project with no `:paths` ↳ `:include` passes validation. A test using `TEST_INCLUDE_PATH(include)` built and passed. The same project without the macro stopped with `Found no file `foo.h` in search paths`.

title: A release build needs :paths :test although the project file docs list only :build_root and :paths :source
claim: Verdict: broken. A project with `:release_build: TRUE`, `:project` ↳ `:build_root` and `:paths` ↳ `:source`, and no `:paths` ↳ `:test`, stops with `Required config file entry :paths ↳ :test does not exist.` The check lists `:paths` ↳ `:test` for every build.

title: Second-tier keys ending in _path or _paths get Ruby expansion and standard separators
claim: Verdict: kept. `eval_paths` expands every second-tier key that matches `/_path(s)?$/` under each top-level section, and `standardize_convention_paths` standardizes the same set. `:project` ↳ `:build_root`, :release_build ↳ :artifacts` and `:paths`/`:files` are handled by their own lines.

title: Which Ceedling picks WHICH_CEEDLING, then :which_ceedling, then vendor/ceedling, then the gem, with ~ expanded
claim: Verdict: kept. `InstallationSelector#select` takes the first of the environment variable, the config value and `vendor/ceedling` and falls back to the launcher's own root. `validate` standardizes the value, which expands `~`. Every experiment log here shows `Launching Ceedling from /home/user/Ceedling/` from `:which_ceedling`.

title: A relative which-ceedling path and vendor/ceedling are resolved from the working directory
claim: Verdict: kept. The selector checks `vendor/ceedling` and the configured path with `directory?`, which reads relative to the working directory. It never uses the project file's directory.

title: A symlink to the running installation is the same installation
claim: Verdict: kept. `Installation#identity` returns `File.realpath(@root)`, so two spellings of one directory compare equal.

title: A relative release :output is linked below build/release and copied flat into artifacts/release
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say the artifact "is to be found in <build path>/artifacts/release/". With `:output: sub/app.out` the linker output is `build/release/sub/app.out`, and `artifactinate` copies it to `build/artifacts/release/app.out` without the `sub/`. The default name `project.out` is also copied there. `:artifacts` entries are copied to the same directory.

title: An absolute or ~ release :output names the release itself
claim: Verdict: kept. `release_place` keeps an absolute name as written and joins any other below the release root. `~` is expanded by `ProjectPaths.standardize`. Builds with an absolute `:output` and a `~/...` `:output` linked to those paths and still copied to `build/artifacts/release/app.out`.

title: The release-build doc example names build/release/out/c/, which the layout does not use
claim: Verdict: broken (illustrative). The `:artifacts` example is `build/release/out/c/top_secret.s19`. Release objects sit at `build/release/out/<source directory>/<name>.o` (`build/release/out/src/main.o`, `.../src/drv/led.o`). No `c/` directory exists.

title: The :extension lists name output files by their first entry
claim: Verdict: partly kept. Each type accepts a list and Ceedling collects files under any of them. Derived output names (objects, dependency files, maps) use `.primary`, the first entry, so a second entry never names an output.

title: Unity runner :includes entries are written to the runner as typed
claim: Verdict: kept. With `:test_runner` ↳ `:includes: [foo.h, sub/missing.h]` the runner holds `#include "foo.h"` and `#include "sub/missing.h"`, and the compiler finds both through the `:include` path.

title: The ${5} search path list holds more than the :paths and path-macro entries the tools doc names
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The doc says `-I"${5}"` expands to the search paths of `:paths` plus build directive path macros. The real test compile line puts the test's mocks root, Partials roots and each Partial subdirectory first, then `:include` entries, then the vendor roots. `:paths` ↳ `:test` and ↳ `:source` directories are not on it.

title: The tools doc's compile and link examples show a layout Ceedling does not build
claim: Verdict: broken (illustrative). The example compile line has `-I"project/tests" -I"project/source"` and outputs `build/tests/out/source.o`. The linker example writes `build\tests\out\test_thing.exe`. Ceedling builds objects at `build/test/out/<test path>/_t_/<mirrored source path>.o`. Source and test directories are not `-I` entries.

title: A tool executable written as a path is checked on disk and a bare name in the system search path
claim: Verdict: kept. `explicit_path?` is true when the executable holds `/` or `\`. Such a name is checked as a file relative to the working directory. A bare name is looked for in the system search paths.

title: compile_commands.json is keyed by the compiled source path and rewrites a temporary copy to its original
claim: Verdict: kept. The plugin writes `<build root>/artifacts/compile_commands.json`. Its in-memory database is keyed by `entry['file']`, the compiled source path, so a later compile replaces an earlier one. A same-named pair of generated Partials gets two entries (`.../_t_/a/ceedling_partial_util_impl.c`, `.../_t_/b/...`). A compile of a temporary copy has the copy's path replaced by the original in the command line.

title: cppcheck:<filename> takes a trailing path and chooses silently among same-named sources
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The docs say "by filename with no path". The rule calls `find_source_file`, which uses the non-strict lookup: a trailing path narrows the match, and an ambiguous name resolves to the first source in collection order with a one-time NOTICE and no error. The `test:` tasks raise on the same ambiguity.

title: Plugin docs spell the default build root where the plugin follows :build_root
claim: Verdict: partly kept. The Cppcheck, Bullseye and Gcov docs print `build/artifacts/...` and `build/gcov/out/`. The plugins build those paths from `PROJECT_BUILD_ARTIFACTS_ROOT` and `PROJECT_BUILD_ROOT`, so the doc paths hold only for `:build_root: build`. Other docs of the same plugins write `<build root>`.

title: Cppcheck report filenames lose any directory and take the plugin's extension
claim: Verdict: partly kept. `form_artifact_filepath` is `File.join(CPPCHECK_ARTIFACTS_PATH, File.basename(filename).ext(extension))`. A configured name with a directory keeps only its basename. `ext` replaces the configured name's extension with the plugin's own (`.sarif`, `.txt`, `.xml`). The docs call each setting a filename and show names with the right extension.

title: Whole-project Cppcheck passes the :paths include and source lists, or none with a project file
claim: Verdict: kept. `generate_reports` passes `COLLECTION_PATHS_INCLUDE` and `COLLECTION_PATHS_SOURCE`, or empty lists when `:cppcheck` ↳ `:project` is set. `:includes` and `:excludes` entries become `--include=` and `-i` options as written. Test-only search paths, generated roots and `TEST_INCLUDE_PATH` entries are not passed.

title: Cppcheck suppression files come from :paths :cppcheck and :files :cppcheck
claim: Verdict: kept. Each `:paths` ↳ `:cppcheck` entry contributes its `*.xml` and `*<extension>` files, a path that does not exist logs a warning, and `:files` ↳ `:cppcheck` revises the list. `files:cppcheck` lists the result.

title: The Bullseye coverage file is test.cov in the working directory
claim: Verdict: kept (the Bullseye behavior itself is untestable here). `BULLSEYE_COVFILE_PATH` is the literal `test.cov`, a path relative to the working directory, which is the project root whenever the project file is loaded from it. The Bullseye claim that sources are stored relative to the file and that this root is the common ancestor was not run.

title: Untested sources compile with the :include collection, matchers keyed by the source's own path
claim: Verdict: kept. Both plugins compile an untested source with `form_test_object_filepath(filepath, context:)`, resolve flags and defines against that source's filepath, and Bullseye passes `collection_paths_include` as its search paths. An object sits below `<build root>/<plugin>/out/` at the source's own directory, so same-named sources in different directories do not share an object. Not run.

title: Gcovr's default exclusions are path-segment patterns built from :paths, :test_file_prefix and :build_root
claim: Verdict: kept. `build_report_exclusions` builds `.*(?:^|/)<test path>/(?:.*/)?<prefix>[^/]+<ext>$` for each `:paths` ↳ `:test` entry, `.*(?:^|/)<support path>/.+<ext>$` for each support entry, and `.*(?:^|/)<build root>/.+\.c$`. The patterns do not start at the project root. A test path `test` also matches `drivers/legacy/test/test_wire.c` and does not match `latest/test_x.c` (a check of the pattern in Ruby; gcovr uses Python's `re`, same for this pattern).

title: ReportGenerator filters are relative ./ globs for test paths and the build root, plus ceedling_partial_*
claim: Verdict: kept. `build_filefilter_exclusions` writes `-./<test path>/**/*` for each test path and `-./<build root>/**/*`. With Partials on, `-ceedling_partial_*` is added. The patterns assume project-relative paths spelled with a leading `./`. The `.gcno` scan skips test-prefixed files anywhere and mocks, runners, `unity` and `cmock` only below the build root.

title: A Partial's #line directives name the module's project-relative source file
claim: Verdict: kept. The generated `a/ceedling_partial_util_impl.c` holds `#line 4 "src/a/util.c"` ahead of the function, the path as the project spells it. The coverage plugins' retargeting of Partial coverage onto the original relies on that path. Not run with a coverage tool.
